artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation plan for the S4 Keyed St-ladder migration and outDegEq field removal.

memory_candidates.content: When a research report falsifies a task description's stated payoff, the plan must re-sequence around the verified payoff rather than preserving the description's ordering. Task 564: the description claimed retiring a duplicated derivation was where the line-count reduction lived; measurement showed that path is net +80 lines across 40 re-verified proof sites, while an unrelated struct-field removal the description treated as optional was worth ~437 lines. The resulting plan put the field removal first (whole payoff, pure deletion of already-proved material) and made the migration purely additive rather than destructive. General pattern for Lean/proof-heavy refactors: a deletion that removes a definition does NOT compound into the proofs when downstream sites depend on the definitional SHAPE rather than the value -- the case splits they perform are required either way, so the deletion buys nothing downstream. Check whether downstream `unfold` sites are shape-dependent before estimating a refactor's reduction.
